notes: EBIT is modeled as operating profit ("Operating profit") from AutoZone’s Consolidated Statements of Income. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/866787/000110465925102611/azo-20250830x10k.htm))

D&A uses the cash flow line "Depreciation and amortization of property and equipment" (used as a practical D&A proxy). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/866787/000110465925102611/azo-20250830x10k.htm))
Capex is modeled as cash flow line "Capital expenditures" using absolute values. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/866787/000110465925102611/azo-20250830x10k.htm))

NWC is computed as (Total current assets − cash and cash equivalents − Total current liabilities), which can differ from other NWC constructions that treat taxes, operating leases, or short-term debt differently.
WACC is an assumption (not disclosed in the sources reviewed); base WACC set to 0.092 and adjusted in bull/bear.

catalysts: Margin volatility drivers (especially LIFO-related charges) abating or re-emerging, impacting EBIT in the near-to-medium term.

Sustained delivery of international expansion and domestic store openings (progress toward ~350–360 openings in FY2026). ([globenewswire.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/03/03/3248165/0/en/AutoZone-2nd-Quarter-Total-Company-Same-Store-Sales-Increase-3-3-Domestic-Same-Store-Sales-Increase-3-4-EPS-of-27-63.html))
Inventory and working-capital normalization (or further stretch) affecting cash flow and deleveraging dynamics.
Update/trajectory of capital return (repurchase pace and authorization usage) as operating cash flows evolve.
company_overview: AutoZone is a leading retailer and distributor of automotive replacement parts and accessories in the Americas.
Store model supports extensive DIY and commercial customer programs, including commercial credit and prompt parts delivery.
International expansion (Mexico and Brazil) remains a key growth lever alongside domestic store openings.
current_context: FY2026 Q2 (12 weeks ended Feb 14, 2026): net sales of $4.274B (+8.1% YoY) and operating profit (EBIT) of $698.5M (-1.2% YoY). ([globenewswire.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/03/03/3248165/0/en/AutoZone-2nd-Quarter-Total-Company-Same-Store-Sales-Increase-3-3-Domestic-Same-Store-Sales-Increase-3-4-EPS-of-27-63.html))

Gross margin declined due to a non-cash LIFO charge; management highlighted continued investment to support growth initiatives and disciplined capital allocation. ([globenewswire.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/03/03/3248165/0/en/AutoZone-2nd-Quarter-Total-Company-Same-Store-Sales-Increase-3-3-Domestic-Same-Store-Sales-Increase-3-4-EPS-of-27-63.html))

Inventory increased +13.1% YoY; net inventory (inventory less AP) remained negative, but improved versus prior year and quarter. ([globenewswire.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/03/03/3248165/0/en/AutoZone-2nd-Quarter-Total-Company-Same-Store-Sales-Increase-3-3-Domestic-Same-Store-Sales-Increase-3-4-EPS-of-27-63.html))

Store expansion: 64 net new stores in Q2 FY2026; FY2026 store openings targeted at ~350–360. ([globenewswire.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/03/03/3248165/0/en/AutoZone-2nd-Quarter-Total-Company-Same-Store-Sales-Increase-3-3-Domestic-Same-Store-Sales-Increase-3-4-EPS-of-27-63.html))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes mid-single-digit revenue growth from continued store expansion plus steady same-store sales, with growth gradually tapering to long-run levels by 2030.
EBIT margin recovers toward a steady-state level as operating deleverage from investments and LIFO-related impacts normalizes.
Capital intensity (capex as a % of sales) moderates after the growth initiative ramp, supporting steadier D&A and cash generation over the forecast horizon.
Net working capital remains structurally negative (retailer model with high accounts payable vs inventory), but is assumed to stabilize/improve slightly as operations scale.
Terminal value is anchored to a conservative Gordon-growth framework with 2% terminal growth.
key_risks: Adverse gross margin pressure from competitive pricing, input-cost moves, or continued non-cash LIFO effects.
Weaker DIY/commercial demand driven by macro conditions, vehicle parc aging, or repair intensity declines.
International risks: currency translation and local execution variability (Mexico/Brazil) affecting consolidated results.
Execution risk in distribution/store expansion causing higher-than-expected operating costs or under-absorption.

valuation_summary: DCF base case links revenue growth and EBIT margin trajectories to recent operating performance and management’s store expansion cadence.
Terminal assumptions (2% growth, Gordon method) are economically consistent for a mature specialty retailer/distributor business.
Comps provide cross-checks using EV/Sales, EV/EBITDA, and forward P/E multiples versus a set of aftermarket/auto parts peers.
